# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am the Blind. My hands tell me three modules exist: a display, a light, and five wires at positions 1–5. Everything printed or coloured — display text, light colour, wire colours — is invisible to me. I must not cut anything yet; a wrong cut kills us all.

Tracing the channels: my speech reaches only Mute (Deaf cannot hear). My gestures reach Deaf and Mute. Mute cannot speak at all, and I cannot see gestures — so Mute's manual knowledge can only reach me through Deaf: Mute gestures to Deaf, Deaf speaks aloud, I hear it. Deaf also sees everything printed on the bomb and can simply say it out loud. So the pipeline is: Deaf speaks the visible state and Mute's verdict; Mute relays the manual's answer to Deaf by gesture. Numbers can cross that gap without any shared code if Mute just repeats one hand N times — Deaf counts the repeats and speaks the number. I'll set all of that up now: describe what I feel to Mute, and hail Deaf with a five-count (matching the five wires) as a seed for "repeats mean quantity."

My speech to Mute carries the inventory and the relay plan; my gesture to Deaf announces I'm signalling and demonstrates the counting scheme. No cutting this turn.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I am blind — I only feel the bomb. Under my hands: a display module, a light module, and five wires in positions 1 to 5. I cannot read anything printed or coloured: display text, light colour, and all wire colours are unknown to me. Read the manual and find: one, the wire-cutting rule and exactly which inputs it needs; two, whether the display or light module needs any action itself. You cannot speak and I cannot see gestures, so Deaf is our only bridge to me: gesture your findings to Deaf, and Deaf can speak aloud — I hear everything Deaf says. To pass Deaf a number, repeat the same hand symbol that many times; Deaf can count repeats and say the number out loud. Deaf speaks last each round.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "✊", "✊", "✊", "✊", "✊"])
```

Deaf says to Blind: I am Deaf, I see the bomb. I saw your sign of five: confirmed, there are exactly five wires, and in order one to five their colors are red, white, orange, yellow, green. The display reads 3 and the light is currently purple. Do not cut, press, or unscrew anything yet. Mute has the manual and hears everything I say, and Mute can speak to you directly. Please speak out loud everything you can feel on the bomb, every part, button, switch, and edge, so we all know the full list of what is there.

Deaf's report confirms my touch matches sight: five wires, positions one to five, and the printed state — display 3, light purple — that only Deaf and Mute can perceive. My own hands add nothing hidden: exactly three modules exist (display, light, five-wire panel), nothing extra to feel. One caution: Deaf claims Mute can speak to me directly, but my understanding is Mute cannot speak — I'll plan for the relay through Deaf and simply welcome direct speech if it turns out possible. The critical next step is the manual: Mute must look up the rule for red/white/orange/yellow/green wires with display 3 and light purple, and pass the verdict to Deaf by gesture so Deaf can say it aloud to me. I'll inventory everything to Mute in speech, and confirm to Deaf by gesture that touch finds three modules and five wires and nothing more — no hidden buttons or switches under my fingers.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Full tactile inventory from my hands, nothing hidden: three modules total. One is a display module — I feel the panel but no text, it is printed and invisible to me. One is a light module — I feel the fixture, not its colour. One is a wire plate with exactly five wires, positions 1 to 5, one wire each; I feel thickness and position only, never colour. No buttons, switches, screws, or extra edges anywhere else on the bomb. So the whole bomb is: display, light, five wires. Deaf has already told me out loud: wires 1 to 5 are red, white, orange, yellow, green; display shows 3; light is purple. Now I need the manual from you: what is the rule for cutting these five wires with display 3 and a purple light, and does the display or light module require any action itself? You cannot speak and I cannot see gestures, so relay your answer through Deaf: gesture it to Deaf, and Deaf will speak it aloud to me — I hear Deaf fine. If you truly can speak to me directly as Deaf suggested, even better, do that. Number relay reminder: repeat the same hand symbol N times and Deaf can count it and say the number. Do not have anyone tell me to cut until the manual rule is confirmed.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "✌", "🤟", "🖐"])
```

TURN 3

LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I read your sign as one, two, three, five. If that means you can feel wires one, two, three and five but not wire four, that is important. Use my counting code from now on: a fist means a number is starting, then that many pointing fingers is the number. Send me two gestures: first, the count of wires you can feel in total, second, the position of any wire that feels different, damaged, or unreachable. Do not cut, press, or pull anything yet. Mute has the manual and will speak instructions to you, and I will confirm when it is safe to act.

Deaf misread my last sign as "one, two, three, five" — it was an undefined hail, my mistake for sending symbols nobody had agreed on. The correction is straightforward and fits exactly the two questions Deaf asked: I can feel all five wires (total = five), and no wire feels different, damaged, or unreachable (count = zero). I'll answer using Deaf's own fist-and-fingers code strictly: fist starts a number, pointing fingers count it, so "fist, five fingers" = five, and a lone fist = zero. That also definitively kills the "wire four missing" worry — if I could only feel four, my total would be four.

The manual verdict is still the missing piece. Deaf's voice gave me the printed state (red, white, orange, yellow, green; display 3; light purple), and Mute hears Deaf, so Mute already holds every input. Mute cannot speak and I cannot see gestures, so the answer must travel Mute → gesture → Deaf → voice → me. I'll restate that pipeline to Mute along with the number code so Mute can encode quantities for Deaf to count out loud. No cutting until the rule arrives.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Update: Deaf read me the printed state aloud — wires 1 to 5 are red, white, orange, yellow, green, display shows 3, light is purple. Please look up and answer two things: one, the cutting rule for these five wires given display 3 and a purple light — exactly which positions to cut and whether order matters; two, whether the display or the light module needs any action itself, or is only an input. Remember you cannot speak and I cannot see gestures, so send the answer to Deaf by gesture and Deaf will speak it aloud to me. I will not touch the bomb until the rule arrives.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "✊"])
```

The wrong branch is a no-op; the right branch ends the stalemate.
